title: document and document_field are P5's while the legacy document extract and its AC1 and AC3 sit on the P1 slice, and no source gives the extract's source, format or handover
source: Ownership Map v1 document and document_field (owner P5); WP B-P1-05 story line RWB-P1-DM010-APP; legacy RWB-DM-010 Data table, AC1 and Endpoints
description: The legacy story sits in the P1 Recovery data engine module and migrates recovery_case, document and document_field. The Ownership Map puts document and document_field with P5 rwb-document and recovery_case with P3 rwb-case, so the P1 slice can neither own nor write any of the three tables. The Work Package gives AC1 and AC3 of the legacy key to RWB-P1-DM010-APP and AC2 to RWB-ITG-DM010-ITG. No source says who performs the load into rwb_document, how the handed-over rows reach it, or whether the legacy storage reference of a document is taken over by rwb-document unchanged or re-registered in its own custody record.
evidence: Ownership Map tables.document.owner = P5 and tables.document_field.owner = P5 (basis Architecture v5 slide 41, TSD P5 v2 T3.1); tables.recovery_case.owner = P3; legacy RWB-DM-010 Data table rows document DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-033 and document_field DF-DOC-012 to DF-DOC-035; legacy RWB-DM-010 Endpoints: No endpoint in this story; Architecture v5 slide 32: one-off bulk work through service APIs, never their schemas.
proposed: P1 produces the cutover extract of the legacy document and document_field rows with their case, person_key, type, storage reference and confidence, hands it over as a file with a checksum, and rwb-document loads it into rwb_document through its own cutover migration on its own Flyway sequence.

title: The route code sits on the case (P3), the baseline measure snapshots with rwb-reporting (P9) and the case list row with P1, and no source says which side keeps, loads or freezes each of them at cutover
source: Ownership Map v1 recovery_case (P3), measure_snapshot (P9) and case_list_row (P1, ruling ASM-A6-tables-2); legacy RWB-DM-011 Data table and AC1
description: The legacy story migrates recovery_case, case_list_row and measure_snapshot in one P1 cutover step. The Ownership Map splits the three: the case and its route with P3 rwb-case, the measures with P9 rwb-reporting, and the daily case list projection with P1 rwb-source-data. The Work Package gives AC1 and AC3 to RWB-P1-DM011-APP and AC2 to RWB-ITG-DM011-ITG. No source says whether the route history of a migrated case is loaded by rwb-case from a handed-over extract, whether the frozen baseline rows are built by rwb-reporting from events, or whether P1 rebuilds its own case list row for the cutover business date from the legacy rows.
evidence: Ownership Map tables.recovery_case.owner = P3, tables.measure_snapshot.owner = P9, tables.case_list_row.owner = P1 with ruling ASM-A6-tables-2; legacy RWB-DM-011 Data table rows recovery_case DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-055, case_list_row DF-RPT-001 to DF-RPT-019, measure_snapshot DF-RPT-041 to DF-RPT-052; Architecture v5 slides 41 and 44.
proposed: P1 extracts the legacy case list rows, route facts and measure snapshots, loads its own case_list_row for the cutover business date, hands the route facts to rwb-case and the baseline snapshots to rwb-reporting, and copies no COLLINS score.

title: decision_log_entry is P7's and the target writes a local decision record plus the shared topic, while no source says whether the migrated legacy entries are published as records or handed over as a file, or who continues the hash chain
source: Ownership Map v1 decision_log_entry (owner P7); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-03; Architecture v5 slide 41 and the decision-record topic rwb.decision-record.v1; legacy RWB-DM-012 AC1
section: Ownership Map; legacy RWB-DM-012; Arch v5 decision record
description: The legacy story migrates decision_log_entry rows into the monolith's single decision log. In the target a decision record is written locally by the owning service in the same transaction as its state change and is sealed centrally in rwb-decision through rwb.decision-record.v1, and the table belongs to P7. The Work Package gives AC1 and AC3 to RWB-P1-DM012-APP, adds DP-03 with H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, and gives AC2 to RWB-ITG-DM012-ITG. No source says whether historical entries taken outside the Workbench are published as DecisionRecorded events in chain order or handed over as a file for rwb-decision to load, nor which party owns the continued chain after cutover.
evidence: Ownership Map tables.decision_log_entry.owner = P7 (basis Architecture v5 slide 41, TSD P7 v2 T3.1); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-03; Temporal and Drools design slide T5 (chain_seq, prev_hash, entry_hash, JOB-14 at 02:00); legacy RWB-DM-012 Data table decision_log_entry DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031.
proposed: P1 extracts the entries in chain order and emits them through the local decision-record library as DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1 with their original prev_hash and entry_hash; rwb-decision seals them into the central ledger and P1 writes no decision_log_entry row.

title: proceeds is P8's, write_off is S7's and the closure sits on the case (P3) while the legacy money and closure migration is a single P1 slice, and no source says who loads each and what survives of the matching state
source: Ownership Map v1 proceeds (P8), write_off (S7) and recovery_case (P3); legacy RWB-DM-013 Data table and AC1
description: The legacy story migrates recovery_case, proceeds and write_off in one P1 cutover step and reads v_ace_payment and v_ace_write_off. The Ownership Map puts proceeds with P8 rwb-payment, write_off with S7 rwb-writeoff and the case closure with P3 rwb-case, and the split plan gives AC1 and AC3 to RWB-P1-DM013-APP with a second P8 slice RWB-P8-DM013-APP and AC2 to RWB-ITG-DM013-ITG. No source says whether an open proceeds row keeps its matching state through the handover, whether the closure is a case fact or a closure record, or which service sets the write-off committee date on the migrated decision.
evidence: Ownership Map tables.proceeds.owner = P8, tables.write_off.owner = S7, tables.recovery_case.owner = P3 (basis Architecture v5 slide 41); split_plan.json RWB-DM-013 slices [RWB-P1-DM013-APP, RWB-P8-DM013-APP, RWB-ITG-DM013-ITG]; legacy RWB-DM-013 Data table proceeds DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 and write_off DF-FIN-010 to DF-FIN-020.
proposed: P1 extracts the proceeds rows, the closures and the write-off decisions, hands proceeds to rwb-payment and the write-off decisions to rwb-writeoff, hands the closures to rwb-case, and copies no payment and no GL posting.

title: The reference versions, their rows and the lists of values are P3's, the rule rows and their test cases are P7's, and the legacy story names a reference data service that exists in no source
source: Ownership Map v1 reference_version, reference_row and lov_value (owner P3) and rule_package, rule_row and rule_test_case (owner P7); legacy RWB-DM-014 AC1 and AC2
description: The legacy story migrates lov_value, reference_version and reference_row in the P1 Recovery data engine module, and its AC2 has a reference data service validate each version in force and require every rule row to name the test case that proves it. The Ownership Map puts the three reference tables with P3 rwb-case (DP-07) and the rule registry with P7 rwb-decision (DP-04). The Work Package gives AC1, AC2 and AC3 to RWB-P1-DM014-APP, adds DP-07 with H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, and splits no ITG story. No source says which service performs the load, which holds the content hash and the approver of a version, or whether the rule rows and their test cases go to rwb-decision through its registry or through the reference contract.
evidence: Ownership Map reference_version, reference_row and lov_value owner P3 with ruling ASM-A6-tables-5; rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case owner P7 with ruling ASM-A6-tables-3; legacy RWB-DM-014 Data table lov_value DF-REF-027 to DF-REF-033, reference_version DF-REF-159 to DF-REF-180, reference_row DF-REF-181 to DF-REF-184; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-04 and DP-07.
proposed: P1 extracts the versions, their rows and the lists of values and hands them to rwb-case through the published reference-data contract; the rule rows and their test cases go to rwb-decision through its registry; P1 writes no reference row of its own.
